page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-2 is a memory-oriented virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon CPU running at 2.3 GHz on x86_64 architecture. It features 2 virtual CPUs allocated across 1 physical core with 2 threads per core using dedicated CPU allocation. The system is equipped with 13.0 GB of RAM, providing 6.5 GB of memory per vCPU core. Hardware details include 45 MB of L3 cache, 32 KB L1d cache, 0.25 MB L2 cache, and support for AVX, AES-NI, BMI2, and FMA instruction sets. The server includes no local SSD storage and no integrated GPU accelerators.

Performance tests show limited processing and memory throughput across various synthetic benchmarks. The single-core stress-ng test measured 1105.58, while the multi-core score reached 1452.88. Geekbench scores recorded 944.0 for single-core and 1124.0 for multi-core evaluations. Uncached memory read bandwidth recorded 13.32 GB/sec and write bandwidth reached 11.13 GB/sec. Application benchmarks demonstrated a Redis SET processing speed of 1.38 million operations per second and static web serving throughput of 1.58 GB/sec. Small 135M parameter LLM inference yielded 65.37 tokens per second for prompt processing and 37.16 tokens per second for generation.

The 6.5 GB per vCPU ratio offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require higher memory capacity without requiring high vCPU counts. Limited processing power and lack of included local disk space represent key operational tradeoffs. Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-2 is suited for lightweight in-memory key-value caching, basic web applications, small database operations, and low-intensity data processing tasks.
